description: Historical baseline of two distinct probing channels, with temperature. DREAM's 'pixel is real' claim predicts structure resolution flattens at λ_q while field detection goes deeper but finds no structure — only 'shadows' (field fluctuations). The gap between the two channels IS the pixel. DREAM predicts the structure floor does NOT move with temperature — cooling removes thermal noise but not the kernel's resolution limit. If structure resolution improves with cooling → standard physics. If it flattens regardless of T → DREAM supported.

baseline_records.technique: Electron ptychography at liquid nitrogen temp (95K)
LIGO quantum noise — mirror displacement by vacuum fluctuations (40 kg mirrors at room temp, quantum noise is T-independent)
AGIS atom interferometer (ultracold atoms at ~1 μK, projected displacement sensitivity 10⁻¹⁹ m)
NV center in diamond at millikelvin — single-spin field detection
baseline_records.source: Various NV center experiments at mK in dilution refrigerators

baseline_records.technique: Quantum-enhanced LIGO with squeezed light at ~mK (mirror local temp) — sub-SQL displacement

channel_descriptions.structure: Structure resolution — can you resolve spatial features? (microscopy, ptychography, imaging). This is the DREAM 'pixel' channel: beyond this scale, no structure is found.
channel_descriptions.field: Field detection — can you detect field effects without resolving structure? (LIGO quantum noise, atom interferometry, NV centers). These are the 'shadows': field fluctuations at 10⁻¹⁵ to 10⁻²⁰ m where no structure has ever been found.

dream_prediction.claim: λ_q is a structural cutoff of the projection kernel — no engineering improvement can push it lower. The pixel is real.
dream_prediction.no_specific_value: DREAM does NOT predict a numerical value for λ_q. It is a measured constant of our kernel slice (axiom A4), not a derived one.
dream_prediction.two_channel_prediction: Structure resolution curve flattens (saturates) at λ_q. Field detection goes deeper (10⁻¹⁵ to 10⁻²⁰ m) but finds no structure — only field fluctuations ('shadows'). The gap between structure resolution and field detection IS the pixel.
dream_prediction.temperature_prediction: The structure resolution floor does NOT move with temperature. Cooling removes thermal noise (improving field detection) but does NOT improve structure resolution past λ_q. If structure resolution improves with cooling → standard physics, floor is thermal. If it flattens regardless of T → DREAM supported: floor is structural (kernel), not thermal.
dream_prediction.current_status: Structure resolution: 10⁻¹⁰ m at 4K (cryo-EM), 10⁻¹¹ m at 95K (ptychography), 10⁻¹⁴ m at 300K (interferometry). Field detection: 10⁻¹⁵ m at mK (NV), 10⁻¹⁹ m at μK (atom interf), 10⁻²⁰ m at 300K (LIGO). Gap of 4-10 orders of magnitude persists across temperature — consistent with DREAM prediction that the pixel is structural, not thermal.
